section_1.title: Prerequisite: Anatomy of a Planar Graph
section_1.content: Introduce the basic building blocks of a planar graph (a graph that can be drawn without edges crossing). Define Vertices (V), Edges (E), and Faces (F). Crucially, explain that the 'outer' area surrounding the graph counts as one face.
section_1.example: Visualize a simple square. It has 4 dots (Vertices), 4 lines (Edges), and 2 areas: the inside square and the infinite outside world (Faces).

section_2.title: Euler’s Magic Number: V - E + F = 2
section_2.content: Present Euler’s Characteristic Formula as an invariant property of all connected planar graphs. Explain that no matter how you stretch or deform the graph, the alternating sum remains constant at 2.
section_2.example: Show a triangle (V=3, E=3, F=2 -> 3-3+2=2). Add one line dividing the triangle; E becomes 4 and F becomes 3. The formula remains 4-3+3=2 (wait, 3-4+3=2).

section_3.title: The Mirror World: Introducing the Dual Graph
section_3.content: Introduce the concept of 'Duality'. Every planar graph (G) has a 'Shadow' or 'Dual' graph (G*). This is a transformation where roles are swapped: faces become vertices, and vertices become faces.
section_3.example: Imagine a 'Guardian' standing in the center of every face of the original graph (including the outside). These Guardians will become the new vertices of our dual graph.

section_4.title: The Bridge Construction (Transformation Rules)
section_4.content: Demonstrate the step-by-step visual construction of a dual graph. 1. Place a new vertex in every face of the original. 2. For every edge in the original graph, draw a new dual edge connecting the two dual vertices in the adjacent faces.
section_4.example: Animate a cube projected into 2D. Place a 'Red Node' in each of its 6 faces. Draw 'Red Lines' crossing every original 'Black Edge'. The result is an Octahedron—the dual of the Cube.

section_5.title: Duality and Euler: The Mathematical Swap
section_5.content: Connect duality back to Euler's formula. Show that the Dual Graph G* follows its own Euler equation: V* - E* + F* = 2. Reveal the beautiful symmetry: V* = F, F* = V, and E* = E.
section_5.example: Display a table side-by-side. Graph G: V=4, E=6, F=4. Dual Graph G*: V*=4, E*=6, F*=4. The formula stays balanced because the components just swapped labels.

section_6.title: Application: The Maze Runner's Secret
section_6.content: Conclude with a practical application of duality. If we treat the paths of a maze as edges of a graph, the dual graph represents the 'wall-following' logic. Solving the dual graph often reveals the shortest path or the structure of the boundaries.
section_6.example: Character 'Alex' is stuck in a garden hedge maze. By mapping the 'Dead Ends' as vertices in a dual graph, Alex can see the 'Spanning Tree' of the maze and find the exit by never crossing a dual edge twice.

outline.title: The Bridge Construction (Transformation Rules)
outline.content: Demonstrate the step-by-step visual construction of a dual graph. 1. Place a new vertex in every face of the original. 2. For every edge in the original graph, draw a new dual edge connecting the two dual vertices in the adjacent faces.
outline.example: Animate a cube projected into 2D. Place a 'Red Node' in each of its 6 faces. Draw 'Red Lines' crossing every original 'Black Edge'. The result is an Octahedron—the dual of the Cube.

storyboard.title: The Bridge Construction (Transformation Rules)
lecture_lines: First, place a new vertex inside every original face.
Don't forget the vertex for the infinite outer face.
Connect dual vertices if their faces share an edge.
Each original edge is crossed by exactly one dual edge.
The resulting structure is the original's dual graph.
animations: Show a square graph with its dual vertices in faces.
Draw a red #FF0000 edge crossing one original edge.
Complete all red edges connecting the dual vertices.
Highlight the new structure as the 'Dual Graph'.
Show a cube projection transforming into an octahedron dual.

outline.title: Euler’s Magic Number: V - E + F = 2
outline.content: Present Euler’s Characteristic Formula as an invariant property of all connected planar graphs. Explain that no matter how you stretch or deform the graph, the alternating sum remains constant at 2.
outline.example: Show a triangle (V=3, E=3, F=2 -> 3-3+2=2). Add one line dividing the triangle; E becomes 4 and F becomes 3. The formula remains 4-3+3=2 (wait, 3-4+3=2).

storyboard.title: Euler’s Magic Number: V - E + F = 2
lecture_lines: Every connected planar graph follows a mathematical invariant.
Subtract edges from vertices, then add the faces.
This alternating sum always equals exactly two.
Add a vertex and edge; the sum remains constant.
Euler's formula holds regardless of how the graph stretches.
animations: Draw a triangle and label V=3, E=3, F=2.
Display formula 3 - 3 + 2 = 2 in white #FFFFFF.
Add an edge dividing the triangle; update E=4, F=3.
Update formula to 3 - 4 + 3 = 2 and flash #FFFF00.
Add a vertex on an edge; formula becomes 4 - 5 + 3 = 2.

outline.title: The Mirror World: Introducing the Dual Graph
outline.content: Introduce the concept of 'Duality'. Every planar graph (G) has a 'Shadow' or 'Dual' graph (G*). This is a transformation where roles are swapped: faces become vertices, and vertices become faces.
outline.example: Imagine a 'Guardian' standing in the center of every face of the original graph (including the outside). These Guardians will become the new vertices of our dual graph.

storyboard.title: The Mirror World: Introducing the Dual Graph
lecture_lines: Every planar graph has a corresponding dual graph.
Duality transforms faces into vertices and vertices into faces.
This creates a shadow world with reversed geometric roles.
animations: Show a planar graph with 2 inner faces and 1 outer.
Place red #FF0000 dots in the center of all 3 faces.
Label the new red dots as 'Dual Vertices' (V*).
Fade the original graph's vertices to #555555.
Highlight the relationship: 1 Face = 1 Dual Vertex.

Faces are regions bounded by edges, including the outside.

outline.title: Application: The Maze Runner's Secret
outline.content: Conclude with a practical application of duality. If we treat the paths of a maze as edges of a graph, the dual graph represents the 'wall-following' logic. Solving the dual graph often reveals the shortest path or the structure of the boundaries.
outline.example: Character 'Alex' is stuck in a garden hedge maze. By mapping the 'Dead Ends' as vertices in a dual graph, Alex can see the 'Spanning Tree' of the maze and find the exit by never crossing a dual edge twice.

storyboard.title: Application: The Maze Runner's Secret
lecture_lines: Graph duality helps solve complex maze navigation problems.
Dual edges represent boundaries or paths between regions.
Understanding these connections reveals the maze's hidden structure.
animations: Draw a maze structure using grey #888888 lines.
Place blue #0000FF vertices in path regions and exit.
Connect blue vertices to show the solved path.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Bridge Construction (Transformation Rules)", 
            [
                "First, place a new vertex inside every original face.",
                "Don't forget the vertex for the infinite outer face.",
                "Connect dual vertices if their faces share an edge.",
                "Each original edge is crossed by exactly one dual edge.",
                "The resulting structure is the original's dual graph."
            ]
        )

        # Colors
        ORIGINAL_COLOR = GREY_B
        DUAL_COLOR = "#FF0000"  # Red
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW

        # Define Cube Projection (Planar Graph)
        # Outer Square
        v_o1 = self.grid["B1"]
        v_o2 = self.grid["B5"]
        v_o3 = self.grid["F5"]
        v_o4 = self.grid["F1"]
        # Inner Square
        v_i1 = self.grid["C2"]
        v_i2 = self.grid["C4"]
        v_i3 = self.grid["E4"]
        v_i4 = self.grid["E2"]

        orig_vertices_pos = [v_o1, v_o2, v_o3, v_o4, v_i1, v_i2, v_i3, v_i4]
        orig_vertices = VGroup(*[Dot(pos, color=ORIGINAL_COLOR) for pos in orig_vertices_pos])
        
        orig_edges_def = [
            (v_o1, v_o2), (v_o2, v_o3), (v_o3, v_o4), (v_o4, v_o1), # Outer
            (v_i1, v_i2), (v_i2, v_i3), (v_i3, v_i4), (v_i4, v_i1), # Inner
            (v_o1, v_i1), (v_o2, v_i2), (v_o3, v_i3), (v_o4, v_i4)  # Connectors
        ]
        orig_edges = VGroup(*[Line(start, end, color=ORIGINAL_COLOR, stroke_width=2) for start, end in orig_edges_def])
        original_graph = VGroup(orig_edges, orig_vertices)

        # Dual Vertices
        dual_v_pos = {
            "inner": self.grid["D3"],
            "top": self.grid["B3"],
            "right": self.grid["D5"],
            "bottom": self.grid["F3"],
            "left": self.grid["D1"],
            "outer": self.grid["A6"]
        }
        dual_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(pos, color=DUAL_COLOR) for pos in dual_v_pos.values()])
        inner_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(pos, color=DUAL_COLOR) for key, pos in dual_v_pos.items() if key != "outer"])
        outer_dot = Dot(dual_v_pos["outer"], color=DUAL_COLOR)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        self.play(Create(original_graph))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(Create(inner_dots))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        self.play(Create(outer_dot))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(DUAL_COLOR)
        # Connections to the inner face vertex (D3)
        dual_edges_group1 = VGroup(
            Line(dual_v_pos["inner"], dual_v_pos["top"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["inner"], dual_v_pos["right"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["inner"], dual_v_pos["bottom"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["inner"], dual_v_pos["left"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
        )
        # Side connections
        dual_edges_group2 = VGroup(
            Line(dual_v_pos["top"], dual_v_pos["right"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["right"], dual_v_pos["bottom"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["bottom"], dual_v_pos["left"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["left"], dual_v_pos["top"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
        )
        # Connections to outer face vertex
        dual_edges_group3 = VGroup(
            Line(dual_v_pos["outer"], dual_v_pos["top"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["outer"], dual_v_pos["right"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["outer"], dual_v_pos["bottom"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["outer"], dual_v_pos["left"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
        )
        
        self.play(Create(dual_edges_group1))
        self.play(Create(dual_edges_group2))
        self.play(Create(dual_edges_group3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(DUAL_COLOR)
        # Highlight one original edge and its crossing dual edge
        target_orig_edge = orig_edges[4] # inner square edge
        target_dual_edge = dual_edges_group1[0] # inner to top
        
        self.play(
            target_orig_edge.animate.set_color(WHITE).set_stroke(width=6),
            target_dual_edge.animate.set_color(YELLOW).set_stroke(width=6),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            target_orig_edge.animate.set_color(ORIGINAL_COLOR).set_stroke(width=2),
            target_dual_edge.animate.set_color(DUAL_COLOR).set_stroke(width=2),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GREEN)
        dual_graph = VGroup(dual_dots, dual_edges_group1, dual_edges_group2, dual_edges_group3)
        
        label = Text("Dual Graph (Octahedron)", font_size=20, color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(
            original_graph.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.3).set_fill(opacity=0.3),
            dual_graph.animate.set_color(GREEN),
            Write(label)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        graph = VGroup(edge1, edge2, edge3, dot1, dot2, dot3)

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Add a vertex on an edge (edge3: v3 to v1)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Prerequisite: Anatomy of a Planar Graph"
        lines = [
            "Planar graphs are drawn without any edges crossing.",
            "Vertices are points, while edges are connecting lines.",
            "Faces are regions bounded by edges, including the outside."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors for matching lecture lines
        COLOR_L1 = WHITE
        COLOR_L2 = YELLOW
        COLOR_L3 = "#ADD8E6" # Light Blue (matching Face 1)
        COLOR_F2 = "#90EE90" # Light Green
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Planar graphs are drawn without any edges crossing.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_L1))
        
        v1 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        v2 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        v3 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        v4 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(v1, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(v2, "B5")
        self.place_at_grid(v3, "E5")
        self.place_at_grid(v4, "E2")
        
        e1 = Line(v1.get_center(), v2.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        e2 = Line(v2.get_center(), v3.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        e3 = Line(v3.get_center(), v4.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        e4 = Line(v4.get_center(), v1.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        
        graph = VGroup(v1, v2, v3, v4, e1, e2, e3, e4)
        self.play(Create(graph))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Vertices are points, while edges are connecting lines.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_L2)
        )
        
        # Highlight vertices and edges with YELLOW
        self.play(
            v1.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            v2.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            v3.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            v4.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            e1.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            e2.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            e3.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            e4.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
        )
        
        v_label = Text("Vertices", font_size=18, color=COLOR_L2)
        e_label = Text("Edges", font_size=18, color=COLOR_L2)
        
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, "A2")
        self.place_at_grid(e_label, "C1")
        
        self.play(Write(v_label), Write(e_label))
        self.play(Indicate(VGroup(v1, v2, v3, v4)), Indicate(VGroup(e1, e2, e3, e4)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Faces are regions bounded by edges, including the outside.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_L3)
        )
        
        # Face 1 (Inner) - Highlight the inner square region in #ADD8E6
        face1 = Polygon(
            v1.get_center(), v2.get_center(), v3.get_center(), v4.get_center(), 
            fill_opacity=0.5, fill_color=COLOR_L3, stroke_width=0
        )
        f1_label = Text("Face 1 (Inner)", font_size=18, color=COLOR_L3)
        self.place_in_area(f1_label, "C2", "D5") # Centered within the square area
        
        self.play(FadeIn(face1), Write(f1_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Face 2 (Outer) - Highlight the infinite outer region in #90EE90
        # We use a large rectangle for the grid area and treat it as the outer face.
        face2_bg = Rectangle(
            width=6.0, height=6.0, fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color=COLOR_F2, stroke_width=0
        )
        self.place_in_area(face2_bg, "A1", "F6")
        
        f2_label = Text("Face 2 (Outer)", font_size=18, color=COLOR_F2)
        self.place_at_grid(f2_label, "F3")
        
        # Ensure Face 1 and Labels are on top of the Face 2 background
        self.play(FadeIn(face2_bg), Write(f2_label))
        self.add(face1, f1_label, graph, v_label, e_label) # Re-layering
        
        self.wait(2)

section_1.title: Prerequisite: Anatomy of a Planar Graph
section_1.content: Introduce the basic building blocks of a planar graph (a graph that can be drawn without edges crossing). Define Vertices (V), Edges (E), and Faces (F). Crucially, explain that the 'outer' area surrounding the graph counts as one face.
section_1.example: Visualize a simple square. It has 4 dots (Vertices), 4 lines (Edges), and 2 areas: the inside square and the infinite outside world (Faces).

section_2.title: Euler’s Magic Number: V - E + F = 2
section_2.content: Present Euler’s Characteristic Formula as an invariant property of all connected planar graphs. Explain that no matter how you stretch or deform the graph, the alternating sum remains constant at 2.
section_2.example: Show a triangle (V=3, E=3, F=2 -> 3-3+2=2). Add one line dividing the triangle; E becomes 4 and F becomes 3. The formula remains 4-3+3=2 (wait, 3-4+3=2).

section_3.title: The Mirror World: Introducing the Dual Graph
section_3.content: Introduce the concept of 'Duality'. Every planar graph (G) has a 'Shadow' or 'Dual' graph (G*). This is a transformation where roles are swapped: faces become vertices, and vertices become faces.
section_3.example: Imagine a 'Guardian' standing in the center of every face of the original graph (including the outside). These Guardians will become the new vertices of our dual graph.

section_4.title: The Bridge Construction (Transformation Rules)
section_4.content: Demonstrate the step-by-step visual construction of a dual graph. 1. Place a new vertex in every face of the original. 2. For every edge in the original graph, draw a new dual edge connecting the two dual vertices in the adjacent faces.
section_4.example: Animate a cube projected into 2D. Place a 'Red Node' in each of its 6 faces. Draw 'Red Lines' crossing every original 'Black Edge'. The result is an Octahedron—the dual of the Cube.

section_5.title: Duality and Euler: The Mathematical Swap
section_5.content: Connect duality back to Euler's formula. Show that the Dual Graph G* follows its own Euler equation: V* - E* + F* = 2. Reveal the beautiful symmetry: V* = F, F* = V, and E* = E.
section_5.example: Display a table side-by-side. Graph G: V=4, E=6, F=4. Dual Graph G*: V*=4, E*=6, F*=4. The formula stays balanced because the components just swapped labels.

section_6.title: Application: The Maze Runner's Secret
section_6.content: Conclude with a practical application of duality. If we treat the paths of a maze as edges of a graph, the dual graph represents the 'wall-following' logic. Solving the dual graph often reveals the shortest path or the structure of the boundaries.
section_6.example: Character 'Alex' is stuck in a garden hedge maze. By mapping the 'Dead Ends' as vertices in a dual graph, Alex can see the 'Spanning Tree' of the maze and find the exit by never crossing a dual edge twice.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Prerequisite: Anatomy of a Planar Graph"
        lines = [
            "Planar graphs are drawn without any edges crossing.",
            "Vertices are points, while edges are connecting lines.",
            "Faces are regions bounded by edges, including the outside."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors for matching lecture lines
        COLOR_L1 = WHITE
        COLOR_L2 = YELLOW
        COLOR_L3 = "#ADD8E6" # Light Blue (matching Face 1)
        COLOR_F2 = "#90EE90" # Light Green
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Planar graphs are drawn without any edges crossing.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_L1))
        
        v1 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        v2 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        v3 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        v4 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(v1, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(v2, "B5")
        self.place_at_grid(v3, "E5")
        self.place_at_grid(v4, "E2")
        
        e1 = Line(v1.get_center(), v2.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        e2 = Line(v2.get_center(), v3.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        e3 = Line(v3.get_center(), v4.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        e4 = Line(v4.get_center(), v1.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        
        graph = VGroup(v1, v2, v3, v4, e1, e2, e3, e4)
        self.play(Create(graph))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Vertices are points, while edges are connecting lines.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_L2)
        )
        
        # Highlight vertices and edges with YELLOW
        self.play(
            v1.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            v2.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            v3.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            v4.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            e1.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            e2.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            e3.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            e4.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
        )
        
        v_label = Text("Vertices", font_size=18, color=COLOR_L2)
        e_label = Text("Edges", font_size=18, color=COLOR_L2)
        
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, "A2")
        self.place_at_grid(e_label, "C1")
        
        self.play(Write(v_label), Write(e_label))
        self.play(Indicate(VGroup(v1, v2, v3, v4)), Indicate(VGroup(e1, e2, e3, e4)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Faces are regions bounded by edges, including the outside.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_L3)
        )
        
        # Face 1 (Inner) - Highlight the inner square region in #ADD8E6
        face1 = Polygon(
            v1.get_center(), v2.get_center(), v3.get_center(), v4.get_center(), 
            fill_opacity=0.5, fill_color=COLOR_L3, stroke_width=0
        )
        f1_label = Text("Face 1 (Inner)", font_size=18, color=COLOR_L3)
        self.place_in_area(f1_label, "C2", "D5") # Centered within the square area
        
        self.play(FadeIn(face1), Write(f1_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Face 2 (Outer) - Highlight the infinite outer region in #90EE90
        # We use a large rectangle for the grid area and treat it as the outer face.
        face2_bg = Rectangle(
            width=6.0, height=6.0, fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color=COLOR_F2, stroke_width=0
        )
        self.place_in_area(face2_bg, "A1", "F6")
        
        f2_label = Text("Face 2 (Outer)", font_size=18, color=COLOR_F2)
        self.place_at_grid(f2_label, "F3")
        
        # Ensure Face 1 and Labels are on top of the Face 2 background
        self.play(FadeIn(face2_bg), Write(f2_label))
        self.add(face1, f1_label, graph, v_label, e_label) # Re-layering
        
        self.wait(2)

        COLOR_V = "#88CCFF"
        COLOR_E = "#FF8888"

        v_i3 = self.grid["E4"]

            (v_i1, v_i2), (v_i2, v_i3), (v_i3, v_i4), (v_i4, v_i1), # Inner

        ]
        orig_edges = VGroup(*[Line(start, end, color=ORIGINAL_COLOR, stroke_width=2) for start, end in orig_edges_def])
        original_graph = VGroup(orig_edges, orig_vertices)

        # Dual Vertices

            "inner": self.grid["D3"],
            "top": self.grid["B3"],
            "right": self.grid["D5"],
            "bottom": self.grid["F3"],
            "left": self.grid["D1"],
            "outer": self.grid["A6"]
        }
        dual_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(pos, color=DUAL_COLOR) for pos in dual_v_pos.values()])

        self.play(Create(outer_dot))

        # Connections to the inner face vertex (D3)
        dual_edges_group1 = VGroup(
            Line(dual_v_pos["inner"], dual_v_pos["top"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["inner"], dual_v_pos["right"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["inner"], dual_v_pos["bottom"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["inner"], dual_v_pos["left"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
        )
        # Side connections

            Line(dual_v_pos["top"], dual_v_pos["right"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["right"], dual_v_pos["bottom"], color=DUAL_COLOR),

            Line(dual_v_pos["outer"], dual_v_pos["left"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
        )

        ]
        self.setup_layout("Duality and Euler: The Mathematical Swap", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        color_g = BLUE_B
        color_dual = RED_B
        color_swap = YELLOW_A
        color_edge_match = "#00FF00"
        
        # Define Graph G (Tetrahedron projection)

        v_coords_g = [

            center_g + np.array([-0.4, -0.25, 0]),

        ]

        edges_g_indices = [(0,1), (1,2), (2,0), (0,3), (1,3), (2,3)]
        edges_g = VGroup(*[Line(v_coords_g[i], v_coords_g[j], color=color_g, stroke_width=3) for i, j in edges_g_indices])
        
        graph_g = VGroup(edges_g, dots_g)
        label_g = Text("Original G", font_size=20, color=color_g)

            center_dual + np.array([0.35, 0.2, 0]),

        edges_dual_indices = [(0,1), (1,2), (2,0), (0,3), (1,3), (2,3)]

        table_e = Text("E = 6", font_size=24, color=color_g)
        table_f = Text("F = 4", font_size=24, color=color_g)

        table_e_dual = Text("E* = 6", font_size=24, color=color_dual)
        table_f_dual = Text("F* = 4", font_size=24, color=color_dual)
        
        self.place_at_grid(table_v, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(table_e, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(table_f, "E2")
        
        self.place_at_grid(table_v_dual, "C5")
        self.place_at_grid(table_e_dual, "D5")
        self.place_at_grid(table_f_dual, "E5")
        
        # Faces of G
        faces_g = VGroup(
            Polygon(v_coords_g[1], v_coords_g[2], v_coords_g[3], fill_opacity=0.3, color=color_g, stroke_width=0),

            Polygon(v_coords_g[0], v_coords_g[2], v_coords_g[3], fill_opacity=0.3, color=color_g, stroke_width=0)
        )

outline.content: Introduce the basic building blocks of a planar graph (a graph that can be drawn without edges crossing). Define Vertices (V), Edges (E), and Faces (F). Crucially, explain that the 'outer' area surrounding the graph counts as one face.
outline.example: Visualize a simple square. It has 4 dots (Vertices), 4 lines (Edges), and 2 areas: the inside square and the infinite outside world (Faces).

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Prerequisite: Anatomy of a Planar Graph"
        lines = [
            "Planar graphs are drawn without any edges crossing.",
            "Vertices are points, while edges are connecting lines.",
            "Faces are regions bounded by edges, including the outside."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors for matching lecture lines
        COLOR_L1 = WHITE
        COLOR_L2 = YELLOW
        COLOR_L3 = "#ADD8E6" # Light Blue (matching Face 1)
        COLOR_F2 = "#90EE90" # Light Green
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Planar graphs are drawn without any edges crossing.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_L1))
        
        v1 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        v2 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        v3 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        v4 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(v1, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(v2, "B5")
        self.place_at_grid(v3, "E5")
        self.place_at_grid(v4, "E2")
        
        e1 = Line(v1.get_center(), v2.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        e2 = Line(v2.get_center(), v3.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        e3 = Line(v3.get_center(), v4.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        e4 = Line(v4.get_center(), v1.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        
        graph = VGroup(v1, v2, v3, v4, e1, e2, e3, e4)
        self.play(Create(graph))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Vertices are points, while edges are connecting lines.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_L2)
        )
        
        # Highlight vertices and edges with YELLOW
        self.play(
            v1.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            v2.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            v3.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            v4.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            e1.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            e2.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            e3.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
            e4.animate.set_color(COLOR_L2),
        )
        
        v_label = Text("Vertices", font_size=18, color=COLOR_L2)
        e_label = Text("Edges", font_size=18, color=COLOR_L2)
        
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, "A2")
        self.place_at_grid(e_label, "C1")
        
        self.play(Write(v_label), Write(e_label))
        self.play(Indicate(VGroup(v1, v2, v3, v4)), Indicate(VGroup(e1, e2, e3, e4)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Faces are regions bounded by edges, including the outside.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_L3)
        )
        
        # Face 1 (Inner) - Highlight the inner square region in #ADD8E6
        face1 = Polygon(
            v1.get_center(), v2.get_center(), v3.get_center(), v4.get_center(), 
            fill_opacity=0.5, fill_color=COLOR_L3, stroke_width=0
        )
        f1_label = Text("Face 1 (Inner)", font_size=18, color=COLOR_L3)
        self.place_in_area(f1_label, "C2", "D5") # Centered within the square area
        
        self.play(FadeIn(face1), Write(f1_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Face 2 (Outer) - Highlight the infinite outer region in #90EE90
        # We use a large rectangle for the grid area and treat it as the outer face.
        face2_bg = Rectangle(
            width=6.0, height=6.0, fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color=COLOR_F2, stroke_width=0
        )
        self.place_in_area(face2_bg, "A1", "F6")
        
        f2_label = Text("Face 2 (Outer)", font_size=18, color=COLOR_F2)
        self.place_at_grid(f2_label, "F3")
        
        # Ensure Face 1 and Labels are on top of the Face 2 background
        self.play(FadeIn(face2_bg), Write(f2_label))
        self.add(face1, f1_label, graph, v_label, e_label) # Re-layering
        
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Observe the symmetry between the original and dual graphs.",
            "Original faces become the dual graph's vertices.",
            "Original vertices become the dual graph's faces.",
            "Both graphs share the same total number of edges.",
            "Euler's formula remains satisfied through this perfect swap."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Duality and Euler: The Mathematical Swap", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        color_g = BLUE_B
        color_dual = RED_B
        color_swap = YELLOW_A
        color_edge_match = "#00FF00"
        
        # Define Graph G (Tetrahedron projection)
        center_g = (self.grid["A1"] + self.grid["B3"]) / 2
        v_coords_g = [
            center_g + np.array([0, 0.45, 0]),
            center_g + np.array([-0.4, -0.25, 0]),
            center_g + np.array([0.4, -0.25, 0]),
            center_g + np.array([0, -0.05, 0])
        ]
        
        dots_g = VGroup(*[Dot(p, color=color_g, radius=0.06) for p in v_coords_g])
        edges_g_indices = [(0,1), (1,2), (2,0), (0,3), (1,3), (2,3)]
        edges_g = VGroup(*[Line(v_coords_g[i], v_coords_g[j], color=color_g, stroke_width=3) for i, j in edges_g_indices])
        
        graph_g = VGroup(edges_g, dots_g)
        label_g = Text("Original G", font_size=20, color=color_g)
        self.place_at_grid(label_g, "A2")
        
        # Define Graph G*
        center_dual = (self.grid["A4"] + self.grid["B6"]) / 2
        v_coords_dual = [
            center_dual + np.array([0, -0.4, 0]),
            center_dual + np.array([0.35, 0.2, 0]),
            center_dual + np.array([-0.35, 0.2, 0]),
            center_dual + np.array([0, 0.45, 0])
        ]
        
        dots_dual = VGroup(*[Dot(p, color=color_dual, radius=0.06) for p in v_coords_dual])
        edges_dual_indices = [(0,1), (1,2), (2,0), (0,3), (1,3), (2,3)]
        edges_dual = VGroup(*[Line(v_coords_dual[i], v_coords_dual[j], color=color_dual, stroke_width=3) for i, j in edges_dual_indices])
        
        graph_dual = VGroup(edges_dual, dots_dual)
        label_dual = Text("Dual G*", font_size=20, color=color_dual)
        self.place_at_grid(label_dual, "A5")

        # Table elements - Switched from MathTex to Text to bypass LaTeX installation issues
        table_v = Text("V = 4", font_size=24, color=color_g)
        table_e = Text("E = 6", font_size=24, color=color_g)
        table_f = Text("F = 4", font_size=24, color=color_g)
        
        table_v_dual = Text("V* = 4", font_size=24, color=color_dual)
        table_e_dual = Text("E* = 6", font_size=24, color=color_dual)
        table_f_dual = Text("F* = 4", font_size=24, color=color_dual)
        
        self.place_at_grid(table_v, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(table_e, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(table_f, "E2")
        
        self.place_at_grid(table_v_dual, "C5")
        self.place_at_grid(table_e_dual, "D5")
        self.place_at_grid(table_f_dual, "E5")
        
        # Faces of G
        faces_g = VGroup(
            Polygon(v_coords_g[1], v_coords_g[2], v_coords_g[3], fill_opacity=0.3, color=color_g, stroke_width=0),
            Polygon(v_coords_g[0], v_coords_g[1], v_coords_g[3], fill_opacity=0.3, color=color_g, stroke_width=0),
            Polygon(v_coords_g[0], v_coords_g[2], v_coords_g[3], fill_opacity=0.3, color=color_g, stroke_width=0)
        )
        
        # Animation
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(
            Create(graph_g),
            Write(label_g),
            Write(table_v),
            Write(table_e),
            Write(table_f)
        )
        self.play(
            Create(graph_dual),
            Write(label_dual),
            Write(table_v_dual),
            Write(table_e_dual),
            Write(table_f_dual)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        arrow_f_v = Arrow(table_f.get_right(), table_v_dual.get_left(), color=color_swap, buff=0.1)
        self.play(FadeIn(faces_g), Indicate(table_f), Indicate(table_v_dual), GrowArrow(arrow_f_v))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        arrow_v_f = Arrow(table_v.get_right(), table_f_dual.get_left(), color=color_swap, buff=0.1)
        self.play(FadeOut(faces_g), Indicate(dots_g), Indicate(table_v), Indicate(table_f_dual), GrowArrow(arrow_v_f))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(
            Indicate(table_e),
            Indicate(table_e_dual),
            edges_g.animate.set_color(color_edge_match),
            edges_dual.animate.set_color(color_edge_match)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.lecture[4].set_color(PINK)
        euler_g = Text("4 - 6 + 4 = 2", font_size=24, color=color_g)
        euler_dual = Text("4 - 6 + 4 = 2", font_size=24, color=color_dual)
        self.place_at_grid(euler_g, "F2")
        self.place_at_grid(euler_dual, "F5")
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(arrow_f_v),
            FadeOut(arrow_v_f),
            Write(euler_g),
            Write(euler_dual)
        )
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Euler’s Magic Number: V - E + F = 2", [
            "Every connected planar graph follows a mathematical invariant.",
            "Subtract edges from vertices, then add the faces.",
            "This alternating sum always equals exactly two.",
            "Add a vertex and edge; the sum remains constant.",
            "Euler's formula holds regardless of how the graph stretches."
        ])

        # Colors for highlighting
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_V = "#88CCFF"
        COLOR_E = "#FF8888"
        COLOR_F = "#88FF88"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Triangle vertices
        v1_pos = self.grid["B2"]
        v2_pos = self.grid["B5"]
        v3_pos = self.grid["D3"]
        
        dot1 = Dot(v1_pos, color=COLOR_V)
        dot2 = Dot(v2_pos, color=COLOR_V)
        dot3 = Dot(v3_pos, color=COLOR_V)
        
        edge1 = Line(v1_pos, v2_pos, color=COLOR_E)
        edge2 = Line(v2_pos, v3_pos, color=COLOR_E)
        edge3 = Line(v3_pos, v1_pos, color=COLOR_E)
        
        graph = VGroup(edge1, edge2, edge3, dot1, dot2, dot3)
        
        # Labels for V, E, F
        v_label = MathTex("V=3", color=COLOR_V, font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, "A2")
        
        e_label = MathTex("E=3", color=COLOR_E, font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(e_label, "C5")
        
        f_label = MathTex("F=2", color=COLOR_F, font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(f_label, "C3") # Inside/near face
        
        self.play(Create(graph), FadeIn(v_label), FadeIn(e_label), FadeIn(f_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        formula = MathTex("V", "-", "E", "+", "F", "=", "2", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "E3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        formula_nums = MathTex("3", "-", "3", "+", "2", "=", "2", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(formula_nums, "E3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(formula, formula_nums))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Add an edge dividing the triangle
        # From v1 to midpoint of edge2
        mid_v2_v3 = (v2_pos + v3_pos) / 2
        edge4 = Line(v1_pos, mid_v2_v3, color=COLOR_E)
        
        # Update labels
        v_label_new = MathTex("V=3", color=COLOR_V, font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(v_label_new, "A2")
        
        e_label_new = MathTex("E=4", color=COLOR_E, font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(e_label_new, "C5")
        
        f_label_new = MathTex("F=3", color=COLOR_F, font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(f_label_new, "C3")
        
        self.play(
            Create(edge4),
            Transform(e_label, e_label_new),
            Transform(f_label, f_label_new)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        formula_nums_2 = MathTex("3", "-", "4", "+", "3", "=", "2", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(formula_nums_2, "E3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(formula_nums, formula_nums_2),
        )
        self.play(Indicate(formula_nums_2, color=COLOR_HIGHLIGHT))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Add a vertex on an edge (edge3: v3 to v1)
        mid_v3_v1 = (v3_pos + v1_pos) / 2
        dot4 = Dot(mid_v3_v1, color=COLOR_V)
        
        # Splitting edge3 into two
        edge3.set_alpha(0) # Hide old edge
        edge3a = Line(v3_pos, mid_v3_v1, color=COLOR_E)
        edge3b = Line(mid_v3_v1, v1_pos, color=COLOR_E)
        
        # Update labels
        v_label_final = MathTex("V=4", color=COLOR_V, font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(v_label_final, "A2")
        
        e_label_final = MathTex("E=5", color=COLOR_E, font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(e_label_final, "C5")
        
        formula_nums_3 = MathTex("4", "-", "5", "+", "3", "=", "2", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(formula_nums_3, "E3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot4),
            Create(edge3a),
            Create(edge3b),
            Transform(v_label, v_label_final),
            Transform(e_label, e_label_final),
            ReplacementTransform(formula_nums_2, formula_nums_3)
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Bridge Construction (Transformation Rules)
outline.content: Demonstrate the step-by-step visual construction of a dual graph. 1. Place a new vertex in every face of the original. 2. For every edge in the original graph, draw a new dual edge connecting the two dual vertices in the adjacent faces.
outline.example: Animate a cube projected into 2D. Place a 'Red Node' in each of its 6 faces. Draw 'Red Lines' crossing every original 'Black Edge'. The result is an Octahedron—the dual of the Cube.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Bridge Construction (Transformation Rules)", 
            [
                "First, place a new vertex inside every original face.",
                "Don't forget the vertex for the infinite outer face.",
                "Connect dual vertices if their faces share an edge.",
                "Each original edge is crossed by exactly one dual edge.",
                "The resulting structure is the original's dual graph."
            ]
        )

        # Colors
        ORIGINAL_COLOR = GREY_B
        DUAL_COLOR = "#FF0000"  # Red
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW

        # Define Cube Projection (Planar Graph)
        # Outer Square
        v_o1 = self.grid["B1"]
        v_o2 = self.grid["B5"]
        v_o3 = self.grid["F5"]
        v_o4 = self.grid["F1"]
        # Inner Square
        v_i1 = self.grid["C2"]
        v_i2 = self.grid["C4"]
        v_i3 = self.grid["E4"]
        v_i4 = self.grid["E2"]

        orig_vertices_pos = [v_o1, v_o2, v_o3, v_o4, v_i1, v_i2, v_i3, v_i4]
        orig_vertices = VGroup(*[Dot(pos, color=ORIGINAL_COLOR) for pos in orig_vertices_pos])
        
        orig_edges_def = [
            (v_o1, v_o2), (v_o2, v_o3), (v_o3, v_o4), (v_o4, v_o1), # Outer
            (v_i1, v_i2), (v_i2, v_i3), (v_i3, v_i4), (v_i4, v_i1), # Inner
            (v_o1, v_i1), (v_o2, v_i2), (v_o3, v_i3), (v_o4, v_i4)  # Connectors
        ]
        orig_edges = VGroup(*[Line(start, end, color=ORIGINAL_COLOR, stroke_width=2) for start, end in orig_edges_def])
        original_graph = VGroup(orig_edges, orig_vertices)

        # Dual Vertices
        dual_v_pos = {
            "inner": self.grid["D3"],
            "top": self.grid["B3"],
            "right": self.grid["D5"],
            "bottom": self.grid["F3"],
            "left": self.grid["D1"],
            "outer": self.grid["A6"]
        }
        dual_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(pos, color=DUAL_COLOR) for pos in dual_v_pos.values()])
        inner_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(pos, color=DUAL_COLOR) for key, pos in dual_v_pos.items() if key != "outer"])
        outer_dot = Dot(dual_v_pos["outer"], color=DUAL_COLOR)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        self.play(Create(original_graph))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(Create(inner_dots))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        self.play(Create(outer_dot))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(DUAL_COLOR)
        # Connections to the inner face vertex (D3)
        dual_edges_group1 = VGroup(
            Line(dual_v_pos["inner"], dual_v_pos["top"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["inner"], dual_v_pos["right"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["inner"], dual_v_pos["bottom"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["inner"], dual_v_pos["left"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
        )
        # Side connections
        dual_edges_group2 = VGroup(
            Line(dual_v_pos["top"], dual_v_pos["right"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["right"], dual_v_pos["bottom"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["bottom"], dual_v_pos["left"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["left"], dual_v_pos["top"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
        )
        # Connections to outer face vertex
        dual_edges_group3 = VGroup(
            Line(dual_v_pos["outer"], dual_v_pos["top"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["outer"], dual_v_pos["right"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["outer"], dual_v_pos["bottom"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(dual_v_pos["outer"], dual_v_pos["left"], color=DUAL_COLOR),
        )
        
        self.play(Create(dual_edges_group1))
        self.play(Create(dual_edges_group2))
        self.play(Create(dual_edges_group3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(DUAL_COLOR)
        # Highlight one original edge and its crossing dual edge
        target_orig_edge = orig_edges[4] # inner square edge
        target_dual_edge = dual_edges_group1[0] # inner to top
        
        self.play(
            target_orig_edge.animate.set_color(WHITE).set_stroke(width=6),
            target_dual_edge.animate.set_color(YELLOW).set_stroke(width=6),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            target_orig_edge.animate.set_color(ORIGINAL_COLOR).set_stroke(width=2),
            target_dual_edge.animate.set_color(DUAL_COLOR).set_stroke(width=2),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GREEN)
        dual_graph = VGroup(dual_dots, dual_edges_group1, dual_edges_group2, dual_edges_group3)
        
        label = Text("Dual Graph (Octahedron)", font_size=20, color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(
            original_graph.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.3).set_fill(opacity=0.3),
            dual_graph.animate.set_color(GREEN),
            Write(label)
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: Application: The Maze Runner's Secret
outline.content: Conclude with a practical application of duality. If we treat the paths of a maze as edges of a graph, the dual graph represents the 'wall-following' logic. Solving the dual graph often reveals the shortest path or the structure of the boundaries.
outline.example: Character 'Alex' is stuck in a garden hedge maze. By mapping the 'Dead Ends' as vertices in a dual graph, Alex can see the 'Spanning Tree' of the maze and find the exit by never crossing a dual edge twice.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from shared state
        title = "Application: The Maze Runner's Secret"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Graph duality helps solve complex maze navigation problems.",

        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors from storyboard
        MAZE_COLOR = "#888888"
        DUAL_COLOR = "#0000FF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        maze_walls = VGroup(
            # Outer Boundary
            Line(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["B5"], color=MAZE_COLOR),
            Line(self.grid["B5"], self.grid["E5"], color=MAZE_COLOR),
            Line(self.grid["E5"], self.grid["E2"], color=MAZE_COLOR),

        v7 = Dot(self.grid["D2"] + np.array([0.5, -0.5, 0]), color=DUAL_COLOR) # Bottom-left cell
        v8 = Dot(self.grid["D3"] + np.array([0.5, -0.5, 0]), color=DUAL_COLOR) # Bottom-mid cell
        v9 = Dot(self.grid["D4"] + np.array([0.5, -0.5, 0]), color=DUAL_COLOR) # Bottom-right cell
        
        dual_vertices = VGroup(v1, v2, v3, v4, v5, v6, v7, v8, v9)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(DUAL_COLOR)
        self.play(Create(dual_vertices), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Connect blue vertices to show the solved path.
        # This shows the structure of the maze.
        
        path = VGroup(
            Line(v1.get_center(), v4.get_center(), color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(v4.get_center(), v7.get_center(), color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(v7.get_center(), v8.get_center(), color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(v8.get_center(), v5.get_center(), color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(v5.get_center(), v2.get_center(), color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(v2.get_center(), v3.get_center(), color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(v3.get_center(), v6.get_center(), color=DUAL_COLOR),
            Line(v6.get_center(), v9.get_center(), color=DUAL_COLOR)
        )

        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(DUAL_COLOR)
        self.play(Create(path), run_time=3)
        self.wait(2)

        # Revert colors to white at the end
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Observe the symmetry between the original and dual graphs.",
            "Original faces become the dual graph's vertices.",
            "Original vertices become the dual graph's faces.",
            "Both graphs share the same total number of edges.",
            "Euler's formula remains satisfied through this perfect swap."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Duality and Euler: The Mathematical Swap", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        color_g = BLUE_B
        color_dual = RED_B
        color_swap = YELLOW_A
        color_edge_match = "#00FF00"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Define Graph G (Tetrahedron projection)
        center_g = (self.grid["B1"] + self.grid["C3"]) / 2 # Moved down slightly from original A1-B3
        v_coords_g = [
            center_g + np.array([0, 0.45, 0]),
            center_g + np.array([-0.4, -0.25, 0]),
            center_g + np.array([0.4, -0.25, 0]),
            center_g + np.array([0, -0.05, 0])
        ]
        
        dots_g = VGroup(*[Dot(p, color=color_g, radius=0.06) for p in v_coords_g])
        edges_g_indices = [(0,1), (1,2), (2,0), (0,3), (1,3), (2,3)]
        edges_g = VGroup(*[Line(v_coords_g[i], v_coords_g[j], color=color_g, stroke_width=3) for i, j in edges_g_indices])
        
        graph_g = VGroup(edges_g, dots_g)
        label_g = Text("Original G", font_size=20, color=color_g)
        self.place_at_grid(label_g, 'A2', scale_factor=0.8) # Issue 33 Fix
        
        # Define Graph G*
        center_dual = (self.grid["B4"] + self.grid["C6"]) / 2 # Moved down slightly
        v_coords_dual = [
            center_dual + np.array([0, -0.4, 0]),
            center_dual + np.array([0.35, 0.2, 0]),
            center_dual + np.array([-0.35, 0.2, 0]),
            center_dual + np.array([0, 0.45, 0])
        ]
        
        dots_dual = VGroup(*[Dot(p, color=color_dual, radius=0.06) for p in v_coords_dual])
        edges_dual_indices = [(0,1), (1,2), (2,0), (0,3), (1,3), (2,3)]
        edges_dual = VGroup(*[Line(v_coords_dual[i], v_coords_dual[j], color=color_dual, stroke_width=3) for i, j in edges_dual_indices])
        
        graph_dual = VGroup(edges_dual, dots_dual)
        label_dual = Text("Dual G*", font_size=20, color=color_dual)
        self.place_at_grid(label_dual, 'A5', scale_factor=0.8) # Issue 33 Fix

        # Table elements
        table_v = Text("V = 4", font_size=24, color=color_g)
        table_e = Text("E = 6", font_size=24, color=color_g)
        table_f = Text("F = 4", font_size=24, color=color_g)
        
        table_v_dual = Text("V* = 4", font_size=24, color=color_dual)
        table_e_dual = Text("E* = 6", font_size=24, color=color_dual)
        table_f_dual = Text("F* = 4", font_size=24, color=color_dual)
        
        self.place_at_grid(table_v, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(table_e, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(table_f, "E2")
        
        self.place_at_grid(table_v_dual, "C5")
        self.place_at_grid(table_e_dual, "D5")
        self.place_at_grid(table_f_dual, "E5")
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE_B)
        self.play(
            Create(graph_g),
            Write(label_g),
            Write(table_v),
            Write(table_e),
            Write(table_f)
        )
        self.play(
            Create(graph_dual),
            Write(label_dual),
            Write(table_v_dual),
            Write(table_e_dual),
            Write(table_f_dual)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Original faces morph into dual vertices
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW_A)
        # Faces of G (visualize them before swap)
        faces_g = VGroup(
            Polygon(v_coords_g[1], v_coords_g[2], v_coords_g[3], fill_opacity=0.3, color=color_g, stroke_width=0),
            Polygon(v_coords_g[0], v_coords_g[1], v_coords_g[3], fill_opacity=0.3, color=color_g, stroke_width=0),
            Polygon(v_coords_g[0], v_coords_g[2], v_coords_g[3], fill_opacity=0.3, color=color_g, stroke_width=0)
        )
        arrow_f_v = Arrow(table_f.get_right(), table_v_dual.get_left(), color=color_swap, buff=0.1)
        self.play(FadeIn(faces_g), Indicate(table_f), Indicate(table_v_dual), GrowArrow(arrow_f_v))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Original vertices become dual faces
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE_B)
        arrow_v_f = Arrow(table_v.get_right(), table_f_dual.get_left(), color=color_swap, buff=0.1)
